chunks: And when you see them, their bodies please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech. As if they are wooden beams propped up, they consider every shout to be against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May God fight them, how are they perverted?

key_terms.الصَّيْحَة: a shout or cry (often of criticism or alarm)
key_terms.خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ: wooden beams propped up (metaphor for emptiness)
key_terms.قَاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ: May God fight them (a curse or invocation against them)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the hypocrites in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the metaphor of 'timber leaned against a wall' (khashabun musannadah) highlights the hypocrites' structural weakness and lack of internal conviction, making them susceptible to collapse at the first sign of pressure. This verse is often cited to illustrate the contrast between outward piety and inner spiritual void, warning believers that their eloquence is merely a tool for deception rather than a sign of faith.
